BiblicalUsage: Nardos is nard, the costly spikenard poured on Jesus in the last week before the cross. In John 12:3 Mary takes a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anoints the feet of Jesus, and wipes His feet with her hair, and in Mark 14:3 a woman in Bethany breaks an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard, very precious, and pours it on His head.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe nard is the smell of worship that costs something, because a pound of it was a year's wages and it was poured out in a single evening; the house was filled with the odour, and the act is remembered wherever the gospel is told.
